    According to recent reports, snow, sleet, ice, and sub-zero temperatures make winter driving unpredictable, and a slide into a snowbank or a dead battery can quickly turn into hours stuck on the roadside. In those situations, a well-stocked emergency kit can keep you warm and safe until you’re able to get moving again.

    To help you prepare, we’ve rounded up 23 essential winter emergency supplies to keep in your car, from traction aids and ice scrapers to jump starters and emergency radios.

    A flat tire on a freezing drive doesn’t have to mean calling for a tow. The Airmoto, our pick for best mini inflator in our best tire inflators guide, weighs just 1.2 pounds and fits in a glove box, meaning you never have to be without it. Dial in your target pressure on the digital gauge, and its built-in battery pushes up to 120 PSI, enough to fill a full-size truck tire.

    According to recent reports, what our tester says: “I was surprised at how long the Airmoto’s battery lasted and by its size. It’s small enough to live in a glove box and still powerful enough to get a low tire back on the road.”—Tom Scalisi, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    Sources indicate that A dependable flashlight belongs in every roadside emergency kit, and the Olight ArkPro fits versatile lighting into a slim, pocket-friendly body. Its 1,500-lumen floodlight illuminates a broad area for roadside tasks, while the 800-lumen spotlight helps you see farther ahead. It also offers USB-C and magnetic charging, plus water resistance for wet-weather use.

    It has been revealed that gloves aren’t optional when you’re scraping windows or digging out tires. As the best multilayer option in our tested winter work gloves guide, these Carhartt gloves combine a waterproof layer with a fleece lining for dryness and warmth on winter roads. The polyurethane palms and fingers provide plenty of grip in the cold, and the long fleece cuff keeps snow from sneaking in.

    What our tester says: “These gloves were very warm and did an excellent job of keeping our hands dry.”—Tom Scalisi, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    When winter weather interrupts your trip, an emergency radio offers a reliable way to follow changing conditions. The Midland ER310, our top pick in our lineup of the best hand-crank radios, receives NOAA weather alerts and AM/FM broadcasts to keep you in the know. Its rechargeable battery can run the radio for up to 32 hours, with a hand crank and AA battery backup providing alternatives when charging isn’t an option. A phone-charging port is a welcome addition in an emergency.

    What our tester states: “The built-in flashlight, multiple charging options, phone charging ports, and durable construction provided everything I could ask for in an emergency weather radio.”—Katie Barton, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    It has been revealed that changing a tire is hard enough without ice underfoot, but keeping a bag of Natural Rapport ice melt in your winter car kit can help you clear a slippery patch quickly. The shaker container makes it easy to spread salt around your tires so you can shovel away the buildup before placing traction mats, sand, or cat litter beneath the wheels.

    Read our full review: Natural Rapport Ice Melt.

    According to recent reports, what our tester notes: “We really loved this ice melt’s shaker container for easy spreading. The larger granules also minimized our need to reapply.”—Zach Lazzari, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    It has been revealed that when you’re stuck in snow, put the car in low gear and accelerate slowly, and sprinkle some kitty litter in the path of your tires. The grains act like gravel, giving the treads something to grip so you can pull out of a rut. A 25-pound bag of Premium Choice’s unscented clay litter is an inexpensive, no-fuss option to keep in the trunk.

    It has been revealed that A loose screw or stubborn fastener can turn a minor roadside problem into a frustrating delay. The Leatherman Wingman puts spring-action pliers, screwdrivers, scissors, and a knife within reach without requiring a full toolbox. As the best overall pick in the best multitools guide, it packs 14 functions into a tool that measures just 3.8 inches closed. Keep it in the console for small fixes, cutting tape, or opening packaged emergency supplies.

    What our tester says: “It has all the tools you’re likely to need in a pinch, and they’re easily accessible with minimal effort.”—Glenda Taylor, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    Industry observers note that A good spray de-icer can solve myriad problems. Spray it on the windshield to break up ice and frost—especially useful if your car’s defroster is not in working order—or apply it to headlights and taillights to keep them from freezing over and losing brightness. It’s also a good idea to keep a small container of de-icer like this Ice-Off windshield spray in your bag for those times when your car’s locks freeze over.

    Industry observers note that A snow brush is one of the most essential car accessories to have on hand when winter weather arrives, and the AstroAI combines a snow brush with a 4.5-inch scraper whose built-in knuckles help break up ice on windows. The cushioned foam grip provides a comfortable handhold, and the brush and scraper detach for separate use and compact storage. Featured in our best ice scrapers guide, the fixed-length, 27-inch tool is a practical size to keep in the car for frosty mornings and snowy commutes.

    What our tester notes: “We liked having the brush and scraper together so we could switch between clearing snow and tackling ice. Being able to take it apart also made it easier to stash in the car.”—Glenda Taylor, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    A scraped knuckle or cut can add to the frustration of a winter breakdown, but with the Band-Aid All-Purpose first aid kit in your car, it’s easy to tend to small injuries while waiting for help or fixing a tire. Its 160 pieces provide supplies for minor cuts, scrapes, and burns, while the compact case keeps everything together instead of scattered throughout your glove box.

    An unexpected roadside wait is no time to discover you’re out of water. Fill the Yeti Rambler 64-Ounce Water Bottle before winter trips to keep a half-gallon of drinking water within reach. Its stainless steel construction stands up to everyday knocks, while double-wall vacuum insulation helps maintain the water’s temperature.

    Industry observers note that when slippery conditions leave your tires spinning, these 36-inch polypropylene traction mats provide extra grip in snow, mud, or sand. Each weighs just 2.5 pounds, making them easy to carry and keep in the car for unexpected trouble. While there are several ways to melt ice without salt, these mats take a different approach and make for a fast solution if you find yourself stuck on the side of the road.

    Sources indicate that if a snowbank or ditch has you stuck and mats and a shovel aren’t enough, a tow strap lets another driver pull you free. This Rhino USA strap is 20 feet long and 2 inches wide, with a lab-tested break strength of 20,024 pounds, reinforced loop ends, and a drawstring bag for storage. Attach it only to your vehicle’s designated recovery points, make sure your vehicle weighs less than the strap’s 6,666-pound working load limit, and have the other driver take up slack and pull gradually instead of yanking.

    If you become stranded on the side of the road, the last thing you want is to be uncomfortable and shivering. HotHands Hand Warmers activate when exposed to air, providing up to 10 hours of warmth without batteries, charging, or a working car heater. The compact, single-use packets tuck easily into your emergency kit and slip inside gloves, boots, or pockets to help keep your digits warm during a long wait for roadside assistance.

    Whether you’re putting top snow-shoveling tips to work or driving in icy conditions, the Bogs Arcata II boots are a winter weather must-have. Their waterproof rubber will keep your feet dry in deep snow, and their flexible construction and cushioned footbed make for a comfortable fit. Along with GlacialGrip outsoles for traction on ice, the boots have a Chelsea-style design that makes them easy to slip on and off.

    Whether you’re a passenger on a winter road trip or waiting for roadside help, the Stalwart Electric Car Blanket adds warmth without cranking up the cabin heat. Its soft polyester fleece provides plush lap coverage, while a 96-inch cord reaches back-seat passengers from your vehicle’s 12-volt outlet. The flexible blanket folds for storage in the trunk or back seat. Because it draws power from the car, pack a wool blanket in the trunk as a backup in case the engine won’t run. And if you do idle the engine for heat, clear snow from the tailpipe first so exhaust can’t build up in the cabin.

    Sources indicate that the Rubbermaid 24-Gallon ActionPacker keeps spare food, first-aid supplies, and gear from this list together and easy to find. Its impact-resistant construction stands up to rough handling while the double-walled lid helps protect the contents from getting smashed. Secure latches keep the lid closed to reduce spills and discourage curious dogs, and it doubles as a table or a seat.

    According to recent reports, A shelf-stable protein bar is definitely one of the smartest things to keep in your car, especially when winter weather or car trouble could delay your next meal. The RxBar comes with plenty of protein to stave off hunger for the long haul, and the individual wrapping means you can easily tuck a few into a glove box or your emergency kit. They come in multiple flavor options to please many a preference, though we’re suckers for the peanut butter.

    It has been revealed that A dead battery is frustrating in any season, but winter is an especially unwelcome time to wait for help. Keeping a portable car jump starter on hand lets you jump-start a car without another car, so you don’t have to rely on a passing driver or wait for a tow truck. The USB port on our Noco Boost Sport pick also provides backup power for your phone.

    Recent findings suggest that the AstroAI snow shovel is a handy addition to any emergency supply setup. When snowstorms hit, the telescoping handle extends to three different lengths to help dig you out of trouble, then collapses back down for compact trunk storage. It pairs lightweight aluminum construction with a reinforced iron hinge for added durability. You’ll also get solid stability from the flat shaft and large D-shaped grip, along with a raised blade point designed to break apart thin ice.

    Recent findings suggest that charging your devices can be a lifeline in a winter roadside emergency, and the Marbero Portable Power Station is more than capable of the task. The best lightweight pick in our portable power stations guide, it fits easily in your emergency kit and offers USB-A, USB-C, and AC outputs for charging phones, tablets, and other small electronics.

    What our tester says: “The compact size makes it easy to pack, and the flashlight could genuinely come in handy during a roadside emergency.”—Paul Rankin, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    Help approaching drivers spot your disabled car in snow or fog with the Orion Safety Highway Flare Kit. Its six red flares each burn for 30 minutes and ignite without a lighter or batteries, giving you a dependable warning signal during a roadside emergency. An included high-visibility vest helps make you easier to see when tending to your car, while the heavy-duty polyester carrying bag keeps everything together.

    According to recent reports, A crash, flood, or electrical failure can leave a seat belt jammed and the power windows useless, and this tiny tool is built for exactly that. The resqme has a razor-sharp stainless-steel blade for cutting a jammed belt and a spike for breaking a tempered-glass side window, all in a 1-ounce body. Keep it within reach of the driver’s seat rather than in the trunk, and know that it won’t break laminated glass.

    We may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn More ›.

    Recent findings suggest that snow blowers for gravel driveways aren’t just any ol’ snow blowers. To ensure you clear snow without tossing rocks and dirt around your property, choosing the right type of snow blower for your gravel driveway or walkway is essential. To help you in your decision, we consulted a snow removal expert and tested eight popular snow blowers by plowing over packed and loose gravel.

    Industry observers note that once our testing was complete, we chose the Troy-Bilt Storm Tracker 2890 Snow Blower as our top pick for its adjustable blade height, excellent traction on loose surfaces, and especially wide clearing path. Learn more about how this reliable snow blower machine and the rest of our recommendations performed in our tests, and see which features matter most when choosing among the best snow blowers for gravel driveways.

    It has been revealed that bottom line: Choosing the right snow blower for gravel driveways is crucial. Our top picks offer a range of options for different needs and budgets.

    Sources indicate that before purchasing a snow blower for a gravel driveway, it’s key to understand that not all machines will work for this type of surface. For example, most single-stage snow blowers and electric snow shovels have augers that scrape along the ground. While this design is great for snow removal from smooth pavement, sidewalks, and heated driveways, it doesn’t work well on gravel driveways since it will pick up gravel in addition to snow.

    It has been revealed that while there are many top-rated snow blowers available today, not all are right for clearing a gravel driveway. When selecting the picks for our list, we stuck with models well suited for this type of terrain, namely two-stage blowers. Beyond type, we looked for features that make snow blowers easier to operate, such as push-button starters, heated handles, and sturdy materials that can power through packed snow.

    We tested our selected models by clearing snow from multiple storms in rural Montana, using a loose-substrate gravel driveway and a hard-packed gravel road as our testing grounds. While much of the testing area was level, we also hit a few inclines and ran through mounds of piled-up snow.

    It has been revealed that we rated the snow blowers based on performance in each gravel environment. We looked at skids and adjustments that made it easier to run over gravel, and power, handling, and traction also factored high in the ranking process. Lastly, we assessed build quality, ease of use, battery life, engine performance, and the rest of the nitty-gritty details that make some snow blowers more capable on gravel surfaces.

    Sources indicate that understanding which types of snow blowers are suitable for gravel driveways and which are not is the first step in selecting the right model. Ahead, learn more about the three types of snow blowers as well as other important features, such as power output and intake width.

    There are three main types of snow blowers: single-stage, two-stage, and three-stage. Each one clears snow a bit differently, but for gravel driveways, two-stage models are ideal. Here’s how each of these snow blowers works.

    Like all snow blowers, a single-stage snow blower or snow thrower uses an auger with serrated metal blades to scoop snow and launch it through the chute. Since the auger on this type of snow blower skims along the ground, it’s an excellent option for smooth pavement but a poor choice for loose gravel. If used on a gravel driveway, a single-stage snow blower will gather and throw rocks along with snow.

    Recent findings suggest that similar to a single-stage snow blower, a two-stage model uses an auger to pull snow into the chute. However, rather than use the force of the auger to launch the snow, two-stage snow blowers rely on large impeller fans to propel the snow out of the chute. In addition to being able to throw snow much farther than a single-stage model, a two-stage snow blower’s auger does not come into contact with the ground. Instead of resting on the auger, the snow blower glides on two adjustable skid pads—a design that makes a two-stage model ideal for gravel surfaces.

    Sources indicate that this heavy-duty snow blower uses an auger and impeller fan along with an accelerator, which is  a corkscrew-shaped blade that sits perpendicular to the auger and pulls snow promptly into the machine as it spins. True to its name, an accelerator allows the machine to glide more quickly through snow. These powerful snow blowers can throw snow up to 50 feet away and have intakes that measure up to 40 inches wide. This makes them ideal for covering large driveways. Like a two-stage snow blower, a three-stage model’s auger does not touch the ground, so it’s a good choice for gravel surfaces. Three-stage blowers also come with a hefty price tag. As such, they are typically only needed for regions that see very heavy snowfall.

    Industry observers note that when selecting a snow blower, consider how much power it needs to get the job done. Snow blowers have either a gas engine or, with battery-powered models, an electric motor. A gas snow blower’s power is measured in cubic centimeters. The higher the cc, the better able the snow blower is to move through deeper snow and the farther it can launch it. Two-stage snow blowers for gravel driveways have engines ranging between 200cc and 250cc.

    It has been revealed that electric snow blowers generally use two batteries to maximize runtime, though many can run on one battery (but they won’t run as long). Total runtime varies depending on the voltage and amp hours of the batteries, the number of batteries used, and, of course, the amount and type of snow being cleared. Depending on these factors, many battery-powered snow blowers can run for between 30 and 70 minutes. Some electric snow blowers also have an additional port that enables adding a third battery to extend runtime.

    Sources indicate that although battery-powered snow blowers may not be quite as powerful as gas-powered options, they operate at a much lower noise level and don’t produce exhaust fumes. They also don’t require periodic oil changes, making snow blower maintenance easier. Just keep in mind that lithium-ion batteries typically only last 3 to 6 years before they begin to lose their ability to hold a charge, at which point they need to be replaced. Still, even replacing batteries may be less expensive than paying the cost of snow removal in areas that receive regular snowfall.

    The width of the snow blower refers to the size of its intake and determines how broad a swath of snow the machine can remove with each pass. Most single-stage snow blowers remove snow in 11- to 22-inch swaths with each pass, making them suitable for small driveways and walks. Two-stage models range in width from 22 to 30 inches, making them ideal for most driveways. Large three-stage snow blowers have intakes that measure up to 40 inches wide.

    Some of the best snow blowers for gravel driveways may come equipped with other useful features that make them easier and, in some cases, safer to use, such as:.

    In addition to buying a snow blower rated to work on gravel surfaces, there are other measures you can take to improve performance when clearing snow from this type of surface.

    First and foremost, ensure the skid shoes—the two metal pieces that raise the snow blower intake and auger above the ground—are properly adjusted so that the intake is about 1 inch off the ground. This gap will provide enough clearance between the auger and the ground to prevent it from contacting the gravel.

    If dealing with snow deeper than the height of the auger, consider raising the skid shoes to their highest setting to get the top layer of snow, then lower it to remove the remaining snow.

    Industry observers note that in windy conditions, start blowing upwind on the driveway and set the chute to discharge snow downwind. If the snow is particularly wet, adding nonstick snow blower spray to the chute can help prevent clogging.

    When finished, make sure to clear any remaining snow from the auger to prevent it from freezing and clogging the intake.

This will prevent the machine from picking up and throwing gravel. If you don’t have a snow blower for your gravel driveway yet, check out our guide on clever hacks for how to shovel snow.

    It has been revealed that the best kind of snow blower to use on gravel is a two-stage model. The auger on a single-stage snow blower makes contact with the ground, so it will pick up gravel and throw it. A two-stage or three-stage snow blower has an intake that is elevated above the ground, allowing it to pick up snow without disturbing the gravel beneath it. Three-stage models work similarly, but they are heavy-duty options generally used by professionals.

    They can last 10 years or many more if properly cared for. Snow blower maintenance includes changing the oil (for gas-powered models); lubricating the axle and augers; and periodically checking the shear pins, skid shoes, and belts for wear. Electric snow blowers require battery replacement about every 3 years if used regularly or up to 6 years if used intermittently.

    The best time to get a good price on a snow blower is in either May or June, when manufacturers are introducing new models and demand for these winter-weather machines is low. If you need to buy outside this period, our guide on the best cheap snow blowers offers some excellent options.

    Sources indicate that we asked Thomas Vanneli, founder and CEO of Minneapolis, Minnesota’s Tomms Property Solutions, for advice on this problem. He mentioned, “To avoid scratching concrete, rubber or polymer skid shoes should be installed. Skid shoes stop the metal from coming into contact with the concrete, which will protect it from dings and scratches.” You can also prevent damage to concrete surfaces by adjusting the skid shoes so the intake sits about an inch off the ground.

    Blinds vs. Shades: How to Choose the Right Option for Your Home

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1511 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bobvila

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish

    • In a recent development, blinds and shades are the two popular options, each with their own advantages in interior design and function.

    Sometimes, updating a room can be as simple as updating the window treatments for a quick facelift. The right choice can give you a sleek, modern aesthetic or a softer, more inviting atmosphere. But it’s not all just looks, they also control natural light, maintain privacy, and can even improve your home’s energy efficiency.

    In a recent development, blinds and shades are the two popular options, each with their own advantages in interior design and function. So, which one is right for your space? From design preferences and trends to the practical things like maintenance and insulation, we’ll take a look at the pros and cons of blinds vs. shades to help you find the perfect fit for your home.

    Shades and blinds are both hung within (or just outside) the top of a window frame, and extend to the bottom of the glass pane, but the window coverings differ in the way they’re constructed. Blinds are composed of individual slats made from hard materials like wood, aluminum, or vinyl. These slats can be tilted to control the amount and direction of sunlight entering a room. Most blinds can also be raised or pulled to the side to fully expose the window.

    Sources indicate that window shades, on the other hand, are generally made from a continuous piece of fabric or another flexible material that rolls, folds, or stacks when raised. They give a softer appearance and come in a variety of styles, from light-filtering roller shades to insulating cellular shades.

    Blinds.com’s blackout cellular shade provides privacy and insulation; customize it as motorized, top down/bottom up, or corded/cordless.

    Industry observers note that blinds and shades have their own advantages, so there isn’t an outright winner for every home. Blinds give you more control over light and privacy, while shades can look softer and have insulating properties. Here’s a breakdown of the pros and cons of each.

    The right window treatment depends on more than just how they look. Before deciding between blinds and shades, consider how you use the room, how much natural light you want, and how much maintenance you’re willing to take on. These key factors can help narrow down your options.

    Blinds and shades will both provide privacy, but they each do it differently. Blinds give you more flexibility throughout the day. You can angle the slats to block the view from outside without completely closing off the light from the window. This makes them practical for living rooms, home offices, and other spaces where you want some natural light without feeling exposed.

    Shades give you privacy when they’re lowered, but the amount of privacy will depend on the fabric. Sheer and light-filtering materials can provide privacy during the day, but will show silhouettes at night when your lights are on. Room-darkening and blackout shades are better for bedrooms and bathrooms, where privacy is definitely a must.

    Blinds.com’s premium roller shade blocks UV rays and preserves views, and is available in a variety of patterns, colors, and fabrics.

    Industry observers note that for precise control over how much sunlight gets through the window, blinds have the upper hand. The adjustable slats let you redirect sunlight up at the ceiling or away from a TV or computer screen, reducing glare while still keeping some natural light.

    In a recent development, shades are different. Light-filtering fabrics soften the harsh sunlight and give a gentle glow, while blackout shades are designed to block most incoming light. That remarked, shades don’t really let you fine-tune as much as blinds. For more flexibility, try top-down/bottom-up shades, which can be lowered from the top or raised from the bottom, or dual shades that use both light-filtering and blackout materials.

    Cost for both blinds and shades will depend on the materials, size, and additional features. Basic vinyl or aluminum blinds tend to be the most budget-friendly options, so they’re practical if you’re looking to cover multiple windows without spending a fortune.

    According to recent reports, shades can also be affordable, assuming you’re looking at simple roller shades made from synthetic fabrics. However, premium Roman shades, double-cell cellular shades, and custom fabric options will cost more.

    It has been revealed that for either option, custom sizing, professional installation, and motorized or smart controls can significantly inflate the price tag. Standard-sized, manually operated window treatments are usually the cheapest choice.

    Window treatments can also help keep your home comfortable throughout the year. When it comes to insulation, however, certain types of shades have a clear advantage.

    Sources indicate that cellular shades are particularly effective thanks to their honeycomb construction, which traps air in pockets between the window and the room. This helps reduce heat loss during winter and heat gain during summer, potentially lowering your energy bills. Roman shades with insulating liners can also provide some thermal benefits.

    Sources indicate that blinds can help reduce solar heat gain by blocking or redirecting direct sunlight, but gaps between the slats don’t give you much insulation. If energy efficiency is one of your priorities, well-fitted cellular shades may be your best bet.

    Older blinds and shades have long pull or loop cords, which are a serious strangulation hazard to young children and pets. Luckily, today’s options are much safer, with cordless designs becoming the standard for both blinds and shades.

    There was even an update to window-covering safety standards in June 2024, which restricted hazardous cords on custom window coverings even more. Thanks to this change, you can now choose from a wide range of cordless and motorized options in both categories.

    Recent findings suggest that according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, cordless window coverings are the safest choice for homes with young children. If you still have older cord-operated blinds or shades, replacing them with cordless alternatives is recommended.

    These fabric vertical blinds from Blinds.com filter harsh sunlight and are durable, cost-effective alternatives to drapes.

    Window treatments can have a surprising impact on the look and feel of a room. If you’re wondering how to dress a window without curtains, both blinds and shades give you plenty of stylish options. Blinds have a structured, tailored appearance that works well in modern, minimalist, and traditional interiors. Wood and faux wood blinds can add warmth and natural texture, while aluminum blinds look great in industrial or modern spaces.

    It has been revealed that shades have a little more variety in terms of fabric, color, pattern, and texture. Roman shades can create an elegant, layered look, while simple roller shades are ideal for a clean, understated aesthetic. Woven wood shades made from bamboo or other natural materials can give organic texture and complement coastal, bohemian, or rustic spaces.

    Of course, it will all come down to your own preference and the atmosphere you’re trying to create. Blinds are ideal for a crisp, structured look, while shades can make a room feel softer and more inviting.

    In general, blinds are easier to maintain than shades. The hard surfaces are easy to dust or wipe down with a damp cloth, so they’re a great choice for kitchens, bathrooms, and other areas where moisture or splashes are common. Just keep in mind, though, that cleaning each individual slat can take time.

    Industry observers note that fabric shades need a gentler approach. Most can be vacuumed with a brush attachment, while certain materials can be spot-cleaned. More delicate fabrics may need professional cleaning, and exposure to sunlight can cause some materials to fade over time.

    In a busy house, low-maintenance blinds or easy-clean roller shades may be the most practical options.

    According to recent reports, WIth so many options, the material and configuration you choose can affect everything from durability to how much sunlight enters the room. Here are some of the most common types of blinds to consider:.

    Shades come in a huge range of styles, from simple designs to decorative options that can be more of a focal point in the room. Some of the most popular types include:.

    In a recent development, when choosing between blinds and shades, the decision comes down to what you want in your space. If precise light control, durability, and easy cleaning are your priorities, blinds are probably best. If you prefer a softer aesthetic, better insulation, or room darkening, shades may be worth the extra cost.

    Sources indicate that remember, you don’t have to commit to one type of window treatments and use it throughout the home. Use blinds for high-traffic areas like kitchens and home offices, and shades for bedrooms and living spaces where comfort and aesthetics are more of a priority. Mixing and matching window treatments can help you strike the right balance between style, functionality, and budget.

    This $10 Hardware Store Staple Can Fix More Around the House Than You Think

    • Caulk fixes myriad projects around the house, from outdoor maintenance to indoor decorating.
    • Industry observers note that caulking windows and doors is the best way to reduce drafts, cut home energy costs, enhance your house’s energy efficiency, and decrease your carbon footprint, according to the Consumer Federation of America.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn More ›.

    Caulk fixes myriad projects around the house, from outdoor maintenance to indoor decorating. What makes the material such a versatile DIY essential? The rubbery substance, available in a variety of formulations, including silicone, latex, acrylic, butyl rubber, polyurethane, and construction adhesives, can bond to almost any material, making it a wonderfully flexible material for projects indoors and out. With the right tube of caulk, you can solve just about any problem—including these common concerns.

    Industry observers note that caulking windows and doors is the best way to reduce drafts, cut home energy costs, enhance your house’s energy efficiency, and decrease your carbon footprint, according to the Consumer Federation of America. For this job, choose either acrylic latex or vinyl latex caulk. Acrylic latex caulk works best in dry environments and will perform well for up to 15 years, while vinyl latex can be used in damp areas and lasts about 5 years.

    Concrete and mortar repair caulk is an excellent tool for sealing cracks and gaps in concrete, brick, stucco, stone, and metal. Similarly, it’s perfect for repairing small fissures in foundations and basement walls that allow insects, rodents, and other pests to enter your home. Designed for both interior and exterior use, concrete and mortar repair caulk has a textured finish and can be painted once it’s dry.

    It has been revealed that no matter how carefully you measure and cut, you often end up with little gaps between, above, and below moldings and baseboards. When you need to close the gap, acrylic latex caulk is one of the best caulks for baseboards, ideal for filling in those small spaces. The product dries quickly and can be painted as soon as 6 to 8 hours after application. Acrylic latex also comes in a variety of different pigments, so you can match the color to the surrounding material.

    It has been revealed that over time, small spaces can open up between tiles, and in moist environments that’s an invitation for mold and mildew to grow behind the walls. Both 100 percent silicone caulk and siliconized acrylic caulk are ideal for wet environments and form a durable, watertight seal. Mold- and mildew-resistant silicone caulk is made for nonporous surfaces like ceramic, glass, and metal, while waterproof siliconized acrylic caulk works well on tubs, tile, glass, and ceramic tile surfaces. Gorilla silicone sealant is ideal to use since it is waterproof, and mold and mildew resistant.

    According to recent reports, gorilla silicone caulk is flexible, adheres well, and creates a mold- and mildew-resistant barrier on bathroom surfaces. Read the review.

    In a recent development, when you need to cover small holes and tiny cracks prior to painting, painter’s caulk, an acrylic latex compound, is just what you need. Painter’s caulk such as DAP Alex painter’s caulk adheres to wood, drywall, masonry, and other surfaces. Because it dries to a paintable texture in about an hour, it’s a good choice for busy DIYers.

    Industry observers note that fire barrier sealant, a specialized type of caulk, does more than patch holes. It actually helps make your home safer by preventing fire from moving through open spaces within a structure. Fire barrier sealant can be used to seal holes, gaps, and cracks around holes in interior framing, especially around plumbing or electrical conduits.

    Recent findings suggest that when a length of molding falls off, a corner of carpet comes up, or a tile comes loose, all-purpose caulk can often fix it. Dab a little caulk behind the loose piece, then stick it back into place. You can even use an all-purpose caulk like GE all-purpose silicone caulk to install wood wall paneling without nails.

    Sources indicate that to keep wallpaper from pulling up as it dries, run caulk along all trimmed paper seams, especially in the corners, then smooth with a wet sponge or finger to remove any surface imperfections. For wallpaper that is peeling, lift up the loose section of paper, apply adhesive under it, then smooth the paper back against the wall. Once the adhesive dries, apply a continuous bead of caulk along the seam to keep it from peeling up again.

    With the right caulk, you can even repair a roof! Roof repair caulk, like Roofers Choice Roof Cement Caulk, can be used to seal small cracks or gaps along roof edges, between shingles, and around skylights or flashing. As you might expect, roof repair caulk is completely weatherproof and waterproof, and can be used in wet areas or on dry surfaces.

    Recent findings suggest that as your home’s gutters age, they can develop cracks and gaps, especially around joints and downspout junctions. Butyl rubber caulk, a strong waterproof sealant, can be used to seal joints in those damaged gutters. Dab a little onto the cracks to keep your gutters leak-free—and keep rainwater flowing out and away from your home.

    Sources indicate that painter’s caulk (or decorator’s caulk) is used, as its name suggests, just before decorating and painting. It’s the right choice for sealing crown molding, chair rails, and baseboards because it’s flexible and hides gaps between the wall and the finishes.

    Whether you’re repairing a small hole or a sizable tear in your home’s vinyl siding, siding caulk can help. Simply choose a shade of exterior caulk that matches the hue of your exterior (even black caulk is available), and use a small dab to seal minor punctures, like nail holes. Cover larger holes or tears by applying caulk to the back of a scrap piece of siding, and covering the hole with the scrap piece.

    Sources indicate that caulking between a countertop and a tile backsplash in the kitchen doesn’t just give your work space a “finished” look. It keeps crumbs, food items and worse yet, water, from getting behind your countertop and cabinets. Silicone caulk, which is moisture and mildew resistant, is the best caulk for the job. While you have your caulk gun out, make sure there’s a sturdy seal between your countertop and kitchen sink, too!

    In a recent development, when you don’t have any fluffy furniture pads on hand to stick on the undersides of flower pots and other decorative items, caulk can help. Turn your pots on their sides and apply a few dabs of silicone caulk to the bottoms of the pots. Allow the caulk to dry so the pots won’t stick to your floors. When they’re set, the silicone pads should keep the pot from scratching your hardwood.

    One of the easiest ways to keep your asphalt or concrete driveway in good condition is to attend to cracks as soon as you notice them. The longer you wait, the better the chance that moisture will seep into the cracks, and make an even more fractured-looking mess of your driveway. Load your caulk gun with a quality, water-resistant asphalt crack sealant. Acrylic formulas are flexible and should fit into just about any nook or cranny.

    #32434. It’s Not Too Late to Do the Lawn Maintenance You’ve Been Putting Off

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1229 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Bobvila ↗ Open Full Page

    It’s Not Too Late to Do the Lawn Maintenance You’ve Been Putting Off

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1229 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bobvila

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs.
    • Many people assume lawn care ends when summer does, but autumn is when you’re laying the groundwork for next year’s success, says Allison Koenig, lawn and garden expert at Tractor Supply Company.
    • Earning perfect scores for ease of use, accuracy, and value in our hands-on test, this simple kit can help inform your fall lawn care routine.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn More ›.

    Many people assume lawn care ends when summer does, but autumn is when you’re laying the groundwork for next year’s success, says Allison Koenig, lawn and garden expert at Tractor Supply Company. “The work you do before winter, from mowing and fertilizing to leaf management and soil care, has a much bigger impact on spring performance than most homeowners realize,” she says. We spoke to Koenig and other lawn care experts to learn which fall lawn maintenance tasks you can still do even into early winter to improve the health and appearance of your lawn next spring, and what should be put off because it’s too late.

    Earning perfect scores for ease of use, accuracy, and value in our hands-on test, this simple kit can help inform your fall lawn care routine.

    The biggest misconception about fall lawn maintenance is that the lawn is dead because of cooler temperatures and doesn’t need attention anymore, states Koenig. But this isn’t true; the lawn is just dormant, which is a major difference. “A dormant lawn is still relying on the roots and reserves it built up in fall,” says Koenig. “Treat it like it’s done for the year and skip the prep work, and you’ll feel that mistake in spring.” Just be mindful that once the ground freezes or grass is fully dormant, it’s best to avoid aggressive projects like aerating, heavy raking, and major repairs. Winter is better spent protecting the lawn rather than trying to renovate it.

    Sources indicate that pay a little attention to your lawn in fall and gain the rewards come the busy spring season. Experts suggest the following:.

    According to recent reports, one of the simplest yet most key tasks in fall and winter is to keep your lawn free of debris, says Theresa Smith, senior vice president at NaturaLawn of America in Frederick, Maryland. “Fallen leaves and sticks can smother the grass, block sunlight, and trap moisture, leading to the grass becoming weak and susceptible to disease.” Regularly rake, mulch, and remove any large debris from the lawn to allow your grass to breathe and absorb as much sunlight as possible.

    Mowing the lawn to the right height before winter arrives is an essential fall lawn task for preventing damage, says Smith. “Avoid cutting the grass too short, as this can lead to scalping and weakening the much-needed root system that it needs to survive winter,” she explains. “On the other hand, leaving the grass too long can also damage a lawn if it gets matted down with snow and ice, which can lead to disease and dying off.”.

    Fall is one of the most effective times for weed control because many weeds are moving nutrients into their roots as they prepare for winter, which makes them more susceptible to treatment, notes Brian Feldman, lead agronomist and senior director of technical operations at TruGreen. Consider the timing and the type of lawn, though. “For cool-season lawns, the ideal window is generally October through early November, while warm-season lawns can still benefit from treatment later in the fall, particularly for certain winter annual weeds,” says Feldman.

    Before you put down any fertilizer or aerate, Wells Westmoreland, co-founder of Tomball Lawn Care Service in Tomball, Texas, recommends getting a soil test first. “The results tell you exactly which nutrients your lawn is missing (or has too much of), so when you go to buy fertilizer or hire someone to apply it for you, you’re getting the nutrients your yard actually needs,” he explains.

    According to recent reports, fall can be a great time to aerate and overseed your lawn; however, the best time of year depends on the type of grass you have. “Cool-season grasses, such as Kentucky bluegrass or tall fescue, should be aerated and reseeded in late summer through fall, or mid-August to mid-October,” advises Smith. On the other hand, warm-season grasses, such as zoysias and Bermuda grasses, should be aerated when they are more actively growing, usually during late spring or early summer.

    After a hot and dry summer, lawns begin to recover in the early fall, making it an ideal time to apply fertilizer in support of its growth, claims Smith. “Since daylight hours are shorter, the grass produces less top growth and directs the nutrients in the fertilizer toward root development, which helps keep the lawn healthy during colder months and helps yards that were fertilized to green-up quicker come springtime.” Some states have specific fertilizer restrictions in the late fall months, so be sure to check your state’s regulations before applying fertilizers.

    According to recent reports, although winter typically reduces pest activity, some issues can still arise. Mice, voles, and other small mammals may take refuge in your lawn during the colder months, causing damage by burrowing or feeding on grass roots, warns Smith. “Check for signs of pest damage and act, such as using traps or deterrents if necessary,” states Smith. “Similarly, look for any patches where the grass has turned brown and may be holding disease spores. Rake up the dead grass and bag it so it doesn’t spread before winter temperatures arrive.”.

    Your grass doesn’t need nearly as much water this time of year, so decrease the frequency with which you water it. While you don’t need to stop, it’s a good time to pull back to avoid overwatering, which can cause large patches of your lawn to die off and invite fungus, disease, and root rot, says Westmoreland. “We see this a lot when sprinkler systems are still running on their summer schedule, so be sure to check your timer.”.

    It’s critical to avoid sodding during colder months. “You’ll likely spend several hundred dollars or more hiring a contractor, and the new sod has a very low chance of taking root because it can’t establish itself in the cold,” warns Westmoreland. Instead, wait until spring and you’ll get a much better return on that investment.

    In a recent development, adding a lot of nitrogen right before the cold months encourages latest growth to pop up. “The problem here is that new growth gets hit harder by the cold than more established turf, so nitrogen can end up killing off a big chunk of your lawn,” explains Westmoreland. “Save the nitrogen for when things warm back up; then, the new growth will be supported.”.

    Industry observers note that if you have a warm-season grass like St. Augustine, Bermuda, or zoysia, hold off on aeration and dethatching. These types of grasses only benefit from these processes when temperatures are much higher, as they’ll actively be growing during that time, notes Westmoreland. “In the cold, the root zone on these grass types goes dormant, so aeration will just open up the turf to damage from the cold since the roots won’t be spreading as quickly.” However, if you have cool-season grass like fescue or ryegrass, you can still move forward with these tasks.

    Once soil temperatures have dropped and winter conditions have arrived, it is most likely too late to overseed cool-season lawns, says Feldman.

    The brushless motor delivers up to 486 inch-pounds of torque, while the ½-inch keyless metal chuck accepts larger-shank bits than the ⅜-inch chucks on some entry-level drills. Two speed ranges—0 to 450 and 0 to 1,900 RPM—cover screwdriving and drilling tasks. We found the ten clutch settings prevented overdriving fasteners when assembling furniture or installing hardware, and a separate drilling position provides access to full power.

    In a recent development, we like its compact body, soft-grip handle, and built-in LED—they make the drill a good option for working inside cabinets and other confined spaces. The magnetic bit holder keeps a spare bit within reach, while the battery indicator displays remaining charge. Starting screws may require a light touch on the variable-speed trigger, so the lower gear is useful for more controlled driving. The single included battery suits intermittent household projects, though a spare would help keep longer work sessions moving.

    Get the Black+Decker cordless drill at Amazon, Lowe’s, or Black+Decker.

    The DeWalt DCD1007WW1 is a heavy-duty drill with an efficient brushless motor that produces up to 1,530 watts. Although it was among the more expensive drills we tested, its rugged construction and heavy-duty performance help justify the investment. The kit includes a ½-inch three-speed hammer drill, removable side handle, belt hook, 8-amp-hour battery, charger, and tool bag.

    According to recent reports, we pushed this drill harder during testing, and it delivered. It drilled ½-inch holes in wood faster than any other model we tested, with similarly strong results in steel, brick, and concrete. It also drove every ½-inch lag bolt flush without a pilot hole, then finished driving bolts another drill had left halfway in. After these initial tests, the battery indicator still indicated a full charge. DeWalt claims up to 275 holes per charge.

    This cordless hammer drill was also surprisingly maneuverable thanks to its short motor-and-chuck assembly. Although slightly heavier than the older DeWalt DCD996 we compared it with, it was about an inch shorter. That compact shape helped it fit tighter spaces and feel more balanced when working at different angles. Still, at roughly twice the weight of many 18-volt drills, it is best suited to demanding projects that warrant the extra power.

    Another useful feature is the adjustable LED at the base of the handle. Unlike lights that operate only with the trigger, this one pivots to three positions and can stay on independently for up to 20 minutes. It is brighter than a smartphone flashlight and offers a practical alternative to putting a phone within reach of a dimly lit repair.

    What our tester claims: “The DeWalt 20-volt hammer drill felt like it could do anything, and the shorter nose allowed it to do quite a bit more than its predecessors. It’s incredibly powerful for a cordless drill, and it held a super strong grip on the bit shaft.”—Mark Wolfe, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    Get the DeWalt cordless drill at Lowe’s, The Home Depot, or Acme Tools.

    The standout feature of the Makita 7.2V cordless driver-drill is its hinged body, which converts from a pistol grip to an in-line configuration like an electric screwdriver. We were especially interested in how the straight grip would improve access when using this small cordless drill.

    We began testing with a fully charged battery, the pistol grip, and a small hex-shank paddle bit. The chuck doesn’t accept round-shank bits, which limits bit compatibility. As expected, this 7.2V model lacked the power of the larger drills we tested, but it isn’t intended to compete with a professional 20V drill. It’s designed primarily for drilling wood and drywall, and it handled those tasks well.

    Recent findings suggest that the in-line grip proved most useful when installing fasteners in tight spaces, such as cabinet slides and hinges. In that configuration, the Makita worked like a cordless screwdriver with extra power. Its 21-setting clutch let us adjust the torque to suit different fasteners before disengaging, while two speed settings added versatility.

    If we could keep only one drill/driver for everyday household tasks, we’d choose this Makita. It isn’t a construction drill, but its ability to reach awkwardly positioned fasteners makes it especially useful around the house. It ran for nearly 30 minutes before the battery needed recharging. The LED illuminated the work area and flashed to alert us when the charge ran low.

    Get the Makita DF012DSE cordless drill at Amazon, The Home Depot, or Acme Tools.

    The Ryobi PCL206K2 carries on the brand’s reputation for affordable, dependable tools. This 18V cordless drill has a ½-inch chuck, a maximum speed of 1,750 RPM, and 515 inch-pounds of torque, offering specifications comparable to many higher-priced models while weighing slightly more than 2.5 pounds. The kit includes two 1.5 amp-hour batteries and a charger.

    In testing, the Ryobi delivered impressive drilling and driving speed and power. It bored effortlessly through a 2×4 with a ⅛-inch twist bit, then made a clean, precise hole with a spade bit in just 4 seconds. It was equally quick and effective at driving 3-inch deck screws. Performance nearly matched that of similarly sized brushless drills. We suspect its brushed motor would drain batteries faster, but it held its own in our drilling and driving tests.

    The brushed motor and plastic chuck help explain the lower price. Professional-grade models typically use brushless motors and all-metal chucks for better battery life and durability. For weekend DIYers, though, this standard ½-inch drill delivers ample power and speed at an excellent value.

    Get the Ryobi cordless drill at The Home Depot.

    It has been revealed that the Milwaukee M12 right-angle drill combines useful power with easy access to tight spaces. We tested the kit version, which includes a battery and charger, but those who already own Milwaukee M12 tools can purchase the tool-only model and use their existing batteries.

    Sources indicate that weighing just 2.03 pounds, this compact drill slipped easily into confined spaces and was comfortable to operate with one hand. It lacked the power of some larger models we tested, making it better suited to furniture assembly and drilling small holes than heavy construction work. The built-in LED helped illuminate the work area, although we needed an additional work light in darker spots.

    In a recent development, A welcome feature was the clutch, which helps prevent stripping screw heads when driving fasteners. The elongated trigger also let us shift our grip higher or lower on the handle without losing easy access to the control. For electricians, HVAC technicians, and plumbers who need controlled screwdriving or small-hole drilling in tight spaces, this Milwaukee is a useful option.

    Get the Milwaukee right-angle drill at Amazon (tool only), Ace Hardware (tool only), or The Home Depot.

    Small but mighty, this Bosch cordless drill came with several quick-change attachments that allowed us to drill holes and insert screws in various settings. We swiftly discovered why this Bosch drill features what the manufacturer calls the FlexiClick system: The attachments connect via a simple push-and-click movement that locks them firmly in place. The drill has a standard attachment with a ⅜-inch chuck that accepts most drill and screw bits. It also has an offset attachment that allowed us to adjust the position of the bit to fit in hard-to-reach spots and an angle attachment that gives the Bosch drill a multiposition head for drilling at various slants.

    While this is just a 12-volt model, we found it had ample power and torque to drill holes in dimensional lumber using even a paddle bit. We also found the 20-position clutch helpful for adjusting the torque to keep from stripping out screw heads in both hardwood and softwood.

    The LED guide light isn’t as bright as it could be—it may help slightly, but you will probably want to use a supplemental work light if you’re drilling in low-light situations. The belt clip on this tool is located at the back of the head, which we liked better than the drills with clips located at the base of the handle. It was easier to slip on and off our tool belts. This little drill won’t replace a full-power drill/driver, but it’s an excellent pick for tackling tasks in tight spots.

    Get the Bosch 12V cordless drill at Amazon, Ace Hardware, or Acme Tools.

    Recent findings suggest that we spent 27 hours testing 14 highly rated cordless drills, drilling more than 500 holes and installing 200 screws and bolts. We evaluated drilling speed and power in materials such as wood, steel, brick, and concrete, along with screwdriving control and the ability to seat larger fasteners. We also assessed chuck security, grip comfort, weight, maneuverability in confined spaces, and the usefulness of features such as work lights, speed controls, and adjustable clutches.

    Features such as battery performance and included accessories also informed our value assessments. Each drill received scores from 0 (lowest) to 5 (highest) for build quality, ease of use, performance, and value. We then compared cumulative scores within each voltage range and selected the strongest performers for different users and project types.

    Recent findings suggest that when choosing from different types of drills, start by matching their features to the needs of your projects. The most powerful cordless drill isn’t necessarily the best fit for occasional repairs, especially if its weight makes it tiring to use. As with all the best cordless tools, the ideal tool for the job tends to balance versatility, comfort, and value. Understanding how to use a drill also helps customers get the most out of whatever drill you choose.

    Battery voltage helps indicate a cordless drill’s capabilities, but it doesn’t measure power on its own. Motor design, gearing, and battery performance also matter. When choosing a battery-powered drill, consider the work you plan to tackle rather than voltage alone.

    The distinction between 18V and 20V MAX can be confusing. These labels describe the same voltage class: 20V is the maximum initial battery voltage measured without a workload, while 18V is the nominal voltage. The difference isn’t a startup surge, nor does a 20V MAX label guarantee more power than an 18V model. Similarly, many drills marketed as 12V use batteries rated at 10.8V nominal.

    Use these categories as a starting point:.

    For masonry projects, knowing how to drill into concrete will help you select the appropriate tool, bit, and technique.

    According to recent reports, battery capacity, measured in amp-hours (Ah), also matters. At the same voltage, a higher Ah rating generally means longer runtime, though actual results depend on the drill and workload. Smaller packs keep the tool lighter, while larger packs support longer work sessions but usually add weight and cost. A higher Ah rating alone doesn’t guarantee more drilling power. For occasional projects, a compact battery may be sufficient; for extended use, consider a larger pack or a spare.

    Industry observers note that torque is the twisting force a drill delivers, while speed, measured in revolutions per minute (RPM), describes how promptly the bit turns. A lower gear generally provides more torque for driving fasteners and drilling with larger bits. Higher speeds suit many smaller-bit drilling tasks, though the appropriate speed depends on the material and bit.

    Recent findings suggest that most drills have an adjustable clutch that limits the torque transmitted to the chuck. When resistance reaches the selected setting, the clutch disengages to help prevent overdriving screws or stripping their heads. It responds to resistance rather than a preset screw depth, so choosing the right setting helps maintain control. Knowing how to change a drill bit also helps ensure the bit is properly seated and secured.

    In a recent development, look for at least 10 clutch settings to accommodate different fasteners and materials. A drilling machine with two gear settings offers more versatility, while a variable-speed trigger lets you fine-tune speed within the selected range.

    A drill’s size and weight affect comfort, especially during extended use. Lightweight models can weigh about a pound, while heavy-duty cordless hammer drills may exceed 8 pounds. Extra power often adds weight, so choose a tool that balances capability with comfortable handling. Check whether the listed weight includes the battery, which can make a noticeable difference.

    A compact drill is easier to maneuver in confined spaces, and a smaller body doesn’t necessarily mean less power. Consider both weight and overall dimensions when comparing models.

    Sources indicate that most cordless drills have keyless chucks for quick bit changes. Chuck capacity determines the largest bit-shank diameter the tool accepts, rather than the size of hole it can drill. Many general-purpose models have ⅜- or ½-inch chucks, while some compact drill/drivers use ¼-inch hex holders that accept only compatible hex-shank bits.

    The best drill bits for a project must suit both the material and the drill’s chuck. Check compatibility before buying a bit set.

    It has been revealed that corded drills sometimes come with a brushed motor. They are cheap and reliable, but the brushes eventually wear down and require replacement. Another challenge with brushed motors is that they create friction, which drains the battery faster in cordless models.

    The best cordless power drills often use a brushless motor. These virtually maintenance-free motors use the battery much more efficiently. However, brushless motors cost more. As a result, many budget cordless drills still use brushed motors.

    According to recent reports, for a typical DIYer, the difference is probably negligible. Those who want to maximize performance and runtime, particularly professional owners, often choose a brushless cordless drill.

    Like most modern battery-operated drills, the models in this guide use rechargeable lithium-ion batteries. Runtime depends on battery capacity and workload, while charging time varies with the battery and charger. For extensive drilling, a kit with a spare battery lets you keep working while the depleted pack charges.

    Note that manufacturer runtime claims often factor backup batteries into their runtime estimates. For instance, the specs on a drill that comes with two batteries, each lasting 1 hour, may list a 2-hour runtime.

    In a recent development, additionally, many cordless drills include a smart charger that replenishes the battery faster, usually within 15 to 60 minutes. A charge indicator allows you to monitor battery capacity.

    Depending on your projects, these extras can improve comfort and convenience:.

    A refurbished cordless drill can help you save money or afford a higher-quality model while reducing waste. Unlike ordinary secondhand tools, refurbished models usually undergo inspection, repairs, and testing before resale. Standards vary by seller, however, so check what “refurbished,” “reconditioned,” or “renewed” means for the listing.

    Sources indicate that these tools may come from customer returns or have sustained shipping or warehouse damage. Don’t assume they were barely used or restored to like-new condition. You can browse refurbished drills at Amazon.

    Walmart and other retailers also offer refurbished options. Keep these considerations in mind:.

    Buy from a reputable source and inspect and test the drill promptly after delivery. If something is wrong, you’ll have time to request a return.

    Our in-depth investigation of technologies and specifications above may have you feeling better equipped to choose the best power drill for your needs. That valuable information is underlined by examples of some of the top cordless drills at the moment available. Still, with so many options available, a few questions might remain. The following are answers to some of the most common questions.

    The primary use of a cordless drill is for drilling holes and driving screws. However, you can also get numerous attachments, which are sometimes included in cordless drill sets. Stirrers, for example, can mix paint and other liquids. You can also attach a sanding drum, a wire brush for rust removal, or a polishing bonnet. Our guide covers more uses for your cordless drill/driver.

    Corded models were once more powerful tools. But today, equally powerful cordless models rival them. However, cordless models lose some of their power over the course of the charge, while corded models perform at a consistent level for as long as they’re plugged in.

    An electric screwdriver is usually much smaller, has less power, and cannot drill holes. The cordless drill can drill holes and also drive screws.

    New and improved models enter the market all the time, so it’s difficult to name one brand as the best overall. Bosch, DeWalt, Makita, and Milwaukee all offer tools for different needs and budgets. Comparing individual models—including the best DeWalt drills—is more useful than choosing by brand alone.

    In a recent development, it very much depends on the amp hours of the battery and how hard the drill is working. A battery can last as little as 15 minutes, though many will run between 30 minutes and 1 hour. Buying a spare battery for your rechargeable drill lets you swap it out and keep working while the other charges.

    Brushless electric motors are more efficient and powerful than brushed motors. They often last longer, too. But higher performance also comes at a higher price. For occasional light-duty drilling, brushed cordless drills are more cost-effective.

    The best voltage depends on the user’s needs. For instance, 12-volt drills are inexpensive and perfectly capable of light-duty drilling and driving, while 18-volt drills deliver the higher torque and faster RPM needed for medium- and heavy-duty projects.

    Glenda Taylor is a product tester and writer specializing in construction, remodeling, and real estate. She tests a wide range of power tools as well as other home improvement, household, and lawn-and-garden products.

    Mark Wolfe is a product tester, writer, and serial DIYer. When he isn’t writing, he spends his time upgrading, repairing, and replacing anything and everything in his home, yard, and garden.     #32431. Tech Report: Why Not Seek the Win/Win?

    Tech Report: Why Not Seek the Win/Win?

    📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (540 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Reason

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that "Why not seek the win/win?" Justice Brett Kavanaugh posed that question to Colorado's attorney during last week's oral argument in St.
    • Some background: Colorado operates a universal preschool program that provides public funding for children attending participating schools, including religious schools.
    • According to recent reports, during oral argument, Kavanaugh noted that approximately 2,000 preschools participate in Colorado's program, while only 34 Catholic preschools are involved in the dispute.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that "Why not seek the win/win?" Justice Brett Kavanaugh posed that question to Colorado's attorney during last week's oral argument in St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy, a case involving Catholic preschools and the state's nondiscrimination requirements. His question raises a broader glitch: Why is compromise so difficult in conflicts between religious freedom and LGBTQ rights?

    Some background: Colorado operates a universal preschool program that provides public funding for children attending participating schools, including religious schools. But participating schools must agree not to discriminate on several grounds, including sexual orientation and gender identity. Catholic preschools argue that these requirements interfere with their religious mission, which includes teaching Catholic doctrine about marriage and requiring families to support that teaching. Colorado maintains that religious schools may participate, but must comply with the same nondiscrimination requirements as other schools.

    According to recent reports, during oral argument, Kavanaugh noted that approximately 2,000 preschools participate in Colorado's program, while only 34 Catholic preschools are involved in the dispute. The record does not identify any family headed by a same-sex couple that has sought admission for a child to one of these schools and been rejected. Why couldn't Colorado accommodate these schools while ensuring that other families had ample preschool options?

    Sources indicate that colorado's attorney responded that equal access to publicly funded education requires more than the availability of alternative schools. The Catholic schools have a principled position as well. Why should they have to compromise their religious identity to participate in a generally available public program? They aren't asking Colorado to endorse Catholic doctrine, only to permit them to maintain their religious mission.

    So why is compromise so elusive? St Mary illustrates a dynamic I wrote about in an article several years ago on Masterpiece Cakeshop, another Colorado religious freedom controversy. I argued that conflicts over religious freedom and LGBTQ rights reflect profound cultural divisions in American society. These controversies implicate competing understandings of identity, dignity, and equality.

    For traditional religious believers, marriage and sexuality implicate fundamental religious convictions. Requiring religious schools to disregard those convictions in their admissions policies seems like an intrusion on religious autonomy. For supporters of LGBTQ rights, allowing publicly funded schools to exclude children because of their parents' relationships seems like a denial of equal dignity and citizenship. Each side regards the other's position as demanding a concession on something fundamental. Besides, each side may think it has compromised enough. Colorado doesn't prohibit religious instruction in funded schools; the schools don't ask Colorado to endorse their position on same-sex marriage.

    In a recent development, this isn't the first time the Court has confronted such a problem. About a decade ago in Zubik v. Burwell, Justice Elena Kagan explored possible accommodations in a contraception mandate controversy, and the Court subsequently sought additional briefing on a compromise.

    Industry observers note that kavanaugh's question makes practical sense. The difficulty is that the parties don't understand the controversy primarily in practical terms. Each sees fundamental principles at stake. The Court will resolve the legal dispute in St. Mary. But it cannot resolve the deeper social divisions that make compromises in these cases so difficult.

    I discuss these questions in a new episode of Legal Spirits, available here.

    The Best Right-Angle Drills for Plumbing, Electrical, Cabinetry, and DIY Jobs

    ⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • A right-angle drill solves problems when a standard drill can’t reach—navigating between studs, working inside cabinets, or tackling tight corners.
    • According to recent reports, plumbers, electricians, carpenters, and pretty much anyone involved in construction and renovation projects will appreciate having one handy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that we may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn More ›.

    A right-angle drill solves problems when a standard drill can’t reach—navigating between studs, working inside cabinets, or tackling tight corners. While this makes these specialized power tools handy in these situations, who truly needs a right-angle drill?

    According to recent reports, plumbers, electricians, carpenters, and pretty much anyone involved in construction and renovation projects will appreciate having one handy. Even hobbyists and homeowners may need a right-angle drill when tackling certain jobs, such as installing cabinetry or assembling furniture.

    Sources indicate that we test the top right-angle drills to find the best models for pros and homeowners. Our favorite was the Ridgid thanks to its comprehensive kit, durable build, and impressive power. Below, find the results of our hands-on tests and learn how these models earned their spot in this lineup of the best right-angle drills.

    According to recent reports, any of the following right-angle drills will make it easier to drill holes and drive screws in tight areas, but each one comes with some pros and cons. We’ve detailed both the benefits and the downsides noted during our tests. Some models are best suited to light-duty use, while others are powerhouses designed with construction pros in mind. There’s sure to be one that will suit your project needs.

    Ridgid’s cordless right-angle drill manages to be compact and lightweight while still offering  tremendous drilling and driving power.

    Its head measures just 3.5 inches long, making it one of the shortest 18V or 20V angle drills we tested. Couple that with its slim profile and short length, and it fits easily into tight spaces inside cabinets and under-sink vanities.

    It has been revealed that right-angle drills tend to be top-heavy, which can make them awkward to hold. With its compact size and light weight, the Ridgid was an exception. It felt comfortable and well balanced in the hand, which is significant given that these tools are often used in tight spaces where it’s not possible to get a two-handed grip. Adding to its maneuverability is a long trigger that’s easy to access from various hand positions. The trigger has ample rubberized grip, making it easy to keep a firm hold on the tool.

    Given its smaller size, we expected it to come up lacking in power. It didn’t. With a max speed of 1,900 RPM, the Ridgid had no trouble handling the larger bits we tested, easily boring holes with a 1/2-inch twist bit and 1-inch spade bit. It followed up that impressive performance by effortlessly driving ten 3-inch carpenter screws into a couple of stacked 2x4s. And if you need additional torque, you can get its max 375 in-lbs (inch-pounds) by dropping down to its lower speed setting.

    What our tester indicates: “Ridgid’s right-angle drill is everything you want out of this kind of specialty power tool. It’s compact and lightweight while still packing plenty of power for drilling large holes and driving fasteners.”—Tony Carrick, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    Get the Ridgid right-angle drill at The Home Depot.

    Ryobi’s tools have steadily grown more powerful over the years, slowly closing the gap with premium brands, and the PSBRA02 right-angled drill is a great example of the brand’s progression. With a max speed of 1,700 RPM and 350 in-lbs of torque, it can handle just about any job that requires this type of tool. Those specs also put it in the same ballpark as other cordless drills, all at a friendlier price point for DIYers who may not need premium performance.

    It produced enough power for drilling ½-inch holes with a twist bit and 1-inch holes with a paddle bit. It also didn’t struggle to drive a 3-inch carpentry screw through two 2x4s. The PSBRA02 won’t win any speed tests, but unless you’re drilling dozens of holes or driving loads of screws, you likely won’t notice the time difference.

    The PSBRA02 isn’t the most compact right-angle drill out there, nor is it the largest. Nonetheless, it fits into compact spaces thanks to a head that measures just 3.5 inches long. It also feels comfortable in the hand with a manageable weight, plenty of rubberized grip around the handle, and a long trigger accessible from various hand positions.

    Get the Ryobi right-angle drill at Amazon or The Home Depot.

    It has been revealed that looking for a 12-volt right-angle drill that delivers impressive power? The Milwaukee cordless drill caught our attention for all the right reasons. We tested the kit version of this small right-angle drill, complete with a battery and charger. However, consumers who already own 12V Milwaukee tools can order the drill as a “tool only” and utilize existing batteries.

    This drill sits on the smaller side of the spectrum, weighing in at a mere 2.03 pounds. It slipped effortlessly into tight spots during tests, and its lightweight design let us comfortably operate it with just one hand. Since this drill packs less power than some other models we tested, it isn’t well-suited for heavy construction work. Instead, it excels at light-duty tasks like furniture assembly and drilling small holes in confined spaces. The integrated LED light was handy, though we did use an additional work light in darker areas.

    It has been revealed that the real surprise here is the inclusion of a clutch, an essential feature that prevents stripping screw heads. What’s more, the elongated trigger design allowed us to adjust our grip up or down on the tool handle (based on comfort level) and still easily pull the trigger. While this drill is not intended for heavy-duty tasks, it’s a good choice for electricians, HVAC technicians, and plumbers who require precise screw insertion or minor hole drilling in tight spaces.
